retro.head: 0cbeb5c703a54dc2b1ca96cf28b20b6b034fb4fe
retro.summary: Only fflib_SecurityUtils.cls changed. PMD (23.8→100) came from adding braces (#1), Graph Engine (67.6→100) from an explicit null-check throw in fieldTokenFor (#10), and Limit headroom (51.6→100) mostly from caches, especially the verified-list Set<List<String>> cache (#16), which skips work only because headroomBulkFieldChecks sends identical lists 120 times. Allow/deny results for the tested cases are unchanged, but the evolved code now caches permission outcomes for the whole transaction and resolves error labels once at class load, which no test covers. Resource efficiency (fflib_SObjectSelectorTest, 98.8) did not move.

behaviourChanges.title: Passed field lists skip FLS re-checks for the rest of the transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: Once checkRead/checkInsert/checkUpdate(SObjectType, List<String>) passes for a list, an equal list for the same user, operation and type returns right after the CRUD check, without any per-field FLS evaluation. Revoking permissions mid-transaction (for example deleting a PermissionSetAssignment or PermissionSet field permission inside the same runAs) would be seen by the baseline, which describes again on every call, but not by the evolved code. Only a change of UserInfo.getUserId() invalidates the cache.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In System.runAs(user holding a permission set with FLS on a field): call checkRead(type, [field]) and expect a pass; delete the field permission; call checkRead again and assert FlsException. (First confirm the platform itself re-evaluates within one transaction; if it doesn't, document the cache as matching platform behaviour.)

behaviourChanges.title: DescribeFieldResult cached per type and field name for the transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: The list methods reuse a DescribeFieldResult cached under the type and field name, cleared only when the user changes. Within one user, any permission refresh the platform would show is masked. The single-field and SObjectField overloads still describe fresh each time, so list and single-field calls can disagree after a permission change.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Same as the revoked-permission test, comparing checkRead(type, List<String>) with checkFieldIsReadable(type, String) after the change.

behaviourChanges.title: Exception labels resolved at class load, not at throw time
behaviourChanges.detail: CRUD_MESSAGES and FLS_MESSAGES are static finals initialised when the class first loads, under the user running at that moment. A later System.runAs user with a different language gets messages in the first user's language. The baseline read System.Label inside the exception constructor, so it used the throwing user's language.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Load the class as the admin (call checkObjectIsReadable on Account), then System.runAs a user with LanguageLocaleKey set to another language and a translated label; trigger a CrudException and assert the message equals that user's System.Label value.

behaviourChanges.title: Unbounded heap growth from cloned verified lists
behaviourChanges.detail: Every distinct passing list is cloned into a per-type, per-operation Set and kept for the transaction. Callers that build many different dynamic lists (selectors with varying field sets, large batch jobs) keep growing heap with no eviction. Each call also hashes the whole list for contains(), which is O(n) even on a hit.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call checkRead with 5,000 distinct one-field lists and assert Limits.getHeapSize() stays under a chosen budget, or check the growth is acceptable.

behaviourChanges.title: Unchanged: null, unknown-field and bypass behaviour
behaviourChanges.detail: A null objType still throws NullPointerException (CRUD describe when bypass is off, the fieldTokenFor guard when it is on). An unknown field name still ends in null.getDescribe(), even with bypass on, as in the baseline. Lists are recorded only when bypass is off, and failures are never cached. Recorded here as checked, not as a change.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Assert NullPointerException for checkRead(null, ['Name']) with bypass on and off, and for checkRead(Account.SObjectType, ['NoSuchField__c']) with bypass on.

patterns.title: Verified-list result cache
patterns.detail: A big CPU win on the headroom test, which repeats identical lists 120 times, but it is shaped to the benchmark. Real callers seldom repeat identical lists, and it turns a stateless permission check into a stateful one. Storing a clone and clearing on user change are sound precautions.

patterns.title: Layered caches (single-entry describe, token map, field-describe map)
patterns.detail: Three overlapping caches plus the fflib_SObjectDescribe cache below them. Once the verified-list cache exists, most of their benefit is redundant. They add state and code size for small gains.

patterns.title: Static label maps replacing if/else chains
patterns.detail: Shorter and easier to read, but it moves label resolution to class load (see the language behaviour change).

patterns.title: Shared throw helpers requireObjectAccess / requireFieldAccess
patterns.detail: Removing duplication is good. The field variant's 'pass the describe only when access is denied, else null' argument exists to satisfy coverage and PMD, and reads oddly compared with passing a boolean.

patterns.title: Splitting statements into locals for coverage
patterns.detail: Adds lines only to raise coverage, with no readability gain. Harmless.

patterns.title: Braces on all if bodies
patterns.detail: Plain style improvement, no behaviour change.

patterns.title: Explicit null guard in fieldTokenFor
patterns.detail: Keeps the NullPointerException behaviour and satisfies Graph Engine. It is the one line no test runs.

testGaps.title: Cache invalidation across System.runAs
testGaps.detail: No test calls the same list check as one user and then as a less-privileged user in the same transaction, so a broken resetCachesIfUserChanged would go unnoticed.
testGaps.proposedTest: As the admin, checkUpdate(Account.SObjectType, ['Name']) passes; then System.runAs(read-only user) the same call must throw a CrudException or FlsException.

testGaps.title: READ failures
testGaps.detail: No test fails a read CRUD or FLS check, so the READ message labels and the READ throw path are pinned only indirectly.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a user with no Account read access: assert checkRead(Account.SObjectType, ['Name']) throws a CrudException with getOperation()==READ and the message equal to the formatted fflib_security_error_object_not_readable label; do the same for a read FLS failure on a restricted field.

testGaps.title: Null objType or unknown field
testGaps.detail: The guard's throw line is uncovered, and nothing pins the exception type for bad input.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert NullPointerException for checkFieldIsReadable(null, 'Name') and checkRead(Account.SObjectType, ['Bogus__c']), with bypass on and off.

testGaps.title: Caller changes a list after it passed
testGaps.detail: The stored clone is meant to stop this case passing wrongly, but no test exercises it.
testGaps.proposedTest: As the read-only user, checkRead(Account, fields) passes; add a non-readable field to the same list; the next call must throw FlsException.

testGaps.title: Bypass toggled between calls
testGaps.detail: No test checks that a list passed while bypass was on is not recorded.
testGaps.proposedTest: As the read-only user with bypass=true, checkUpdate(Account, ['Name']); set bypass=false; the same call must throw.

other.title: Headroom test is overfit
other.detail: headroomBulkFieldChecks sends identical lists 120 times, so Limit headroom 100 mainly measures the verified-list cache hit rate. It does not show real per-call cost. Add a variant with fresh or varied lists if headroom should drive future climbs.

other.title: Dimensions that did not move
other.detail: Resource efficiency (fflib_SObjectSelectorTest, 98.8) did not change: its cost is selector SOQL outside this class. Run-time attempts (#23, #24) were discarded. Coverage is capped at 99.5 by the Graph Engine-required throw unless a null-objType test is added.

retro.head: 05aea65402bb7e356ca7f2b433ecdafa3df622fa
retro.summary: Only fflib_SObjectUnitOfWork.cls changed, so it drove every gain. PMD reached 100 through braces and deferred describes (iteration 1), Limit headroom rose 15.4 from skipping redundant resolve passes and removing isResolved() (iterations 5 and 11), and Code coverage rose 4.1 only by deleting untested statements (iterations 3, 8, 10 and 11), with no new paths tested. Tests passing, Graph Engine and Resource efficiency did not move. The main behaviour risk is in the untested external-id relationship path: resolve() now overwrites a parent reference that is already set, and building and validating that reference moved from commit time to register time.

behaviourChanges.title: External-id relationship now overwrites an existing parent reference
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline only called putSObject when Record.getSObject(RelationshipName) was null, so a parent reference the caller set, or an earlier registration for the same field, was kept (first wins). Without the isResolved guard, resolve() always writes the reference stored at registration, so the last registration wins and a manual reference is replaced. Resolve runs in the insert, upsert and update passes, so the overwrite repeats.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Use a mock IDML. Register a Contact as new, register an external-id relationship to Account, then set contact.Account to an Account reference with a different key before commitWork. Assert which reference reaches dmlInsert. Also register the same relationship twice with different ids and assert the first one wins.

behaviourChanges.title: External-id reference built and filled at register time, not commit time
behaviourChanges.detail: relatedObject.newSObject() and put(externalIdField, externalId) now run in Relationships.add. A type-mismatched externalId (for example a String into a number external-id field) throws SObjectException from registerRelationship, outside commitWork's savepoint and onCommitWorkFinished(false), instead of inside the commit. One reference instance is now shared across all resolve passes instead of a fresh one per pass. The new object's type comes from externalIdFieldDescribe.getSObjectType(), which the check just above proves equal to getReferenceTo()[0].
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Register an external-id relationship with an externalId of the wrong type. Assert the exception is thrown by registerRelationship (new behaviour) or by commitWork (baseline), and fix the intended contract.

behaviourChanges.title: Update pass no longer resolves relationships for types without dirty records
behaviourChanges.detail: In the baseline the update pass re-resolved every type. A new child whose parent type was registered later got the parent Id written into the in-memory record (never saved, because the child was not dirty). Now that write is skipped unless the child's type has dirty records, so callers that read the child record's lookup field after commitWork may see null where the baseline showed the Id. Saved data is unchanged.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Create the UoW with types [Contact, Account], registerNew(contact, Contact.AccountId, account) and registerNew(account), commit with a mock DML that assigns Ids, and assert contact.AccountId after commit.

behaviourChanges.title: No 'field not queried' exception for dirty records missing the lookup field
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline isResolved() called Record.get(RelatedToField) whenever the parent had an Id. On a SOQL record without that field this throws SObjectException. Evolved code only calls put, so such records now commit successfully.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Query an Opportunity without AccountId, call registerDirty(opp, Opportunity.AccountId, existingAccount) and commit; assert there is no exception and AccountId is set.

behaviourChanges.title: Same Id written again to already-resolved records
behaviourChanges.detail: Relationship.resolve() and EmailRelationship.resolve() now run on every pass with no guard. Already-inserted records get the same Id written again in the upsert pass, and in the update pass when their type has dirty records. The result is identical; it only costs CPU proportional to links times passes.

behaviourChanges.title: Single-record permanent delete delegates to the list overload
behaviourChanges.detail: registerPermanentlyDeleted(SObject) now wraps the record in a list and calls the list overload, which still calls emptyRecycleBin then registerDeleted. The methods are non-virtual, so a subclass cannot change the dispatch. Behaviour is equivalent, but the single-record path is untested.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call registerPermanentlyDeleted(singleRecord) with a mock DML and assert the record reaches both dmlDelete and emptyRecycleBin.

patterns.title: Brace-wrapping single-statement ifs
patterns.detail: Clears PMD violations with no semantic change.

patterns.title: Mixed DEFERRED and full describes
patterns.detail: Commit-time loops and handleRegisterType use getDescribe(DEFERRED), but every per-record register path still uses the full getDescribe(). Both give the same name, so map keys match, but the inconsistency is confusing. Iteration 14 showed switching the register paths lost headroom. Caching the name per type would be cleaner.

patterns.title: Coverage raised by deleting untested statements
patterns.detail: Coverage rose by shrinking the denominator: locals, fields and statements were removed from the external-id path and the single-record overloads. The untested external-id and publish paths are still untested, so the 83.3% overstates confidence.

patterns.title: Shared registerPublish helper
patterns.detail: Removes duplicated code across the three single-record publish methods with no behaviour change.

patterns.title: Removing isResolved idempotency guards
patterns.detail: Behaviour-preserving and a real CPU saving for Relationship and EmailRelationship, but it silently changed the first-wins/no-overwrite semantics of RelationshipByExternalId.

patterns.title: Eager construction of the external-id reference
patterns.detail: Building the reference in add() mainly served coverage. It moves the failure point and reuses a mutable SObject across passes.

patterns.title: Emptiness guard before resolve in the update pass
patterns.detail: Cheap and clear, and matches the upsert pass, which already checks for records before resolving.

testGaps.title: External-id registerRelationship path is entirely untested
testGaps.detail: The NOTE says no standard object has a usable external Id, but the validation branches and the resolve wiring can still be tested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert each validation message: null relatedToField; Contact.LastName (not a relationship field); Contact.AccountId with Opportunity.Name (wrong object); Contact.AccountId with Account.Name (not an external id). If a test-only custom object with an external-id field can be added, use a mock IDML to assert the Account reference with the external-id value reaches dmlInsert.

testGaps.title: Overwrite and first-wins semantics of external-id relationships
testGaps.detail: Iteration 11 changed these and no test pins them.
testGaps.proposedTest: Register two external-id relationships for the same record and field, commit with a mock DML, and assert which external-id value is used.

testGaps.title: Single-record publish and permanent-delete overloads
testGaps.detail: registerPublishBefore/AfterSuccess/AfterFailureTransaction(SObject) and registerPermanentlyDeleted(SObject) are not run by any test.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a mock IDML with a platform-event type: register one event through each single-record method and assert eventPublish receives it in the right phase. For a single record, assert registerPermanentlyDeleted puts it in both the delete and empty-recycle-bin lists.

testGaps.title: Relationship resolution across type order and passes
testGaps.detail: Nothing tests a child type registered before its parent type, or what the records hold in memory after commit.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use types [Contact, Account] with a Contact-to-Account relationship and no dirty records. Commit through a mock DML that assigns Ids, then assert contact.AccountId and the contents of the dmlInsert lists.

testGaps.title: Dirty records queried without the lookup field
testGaps.detail: This removed failure mode is not pinned by any test.
testGaps.proposedTest: Query an Opportunity without AccountId, call registerDirty(opp, Opportunity.AccountId, account) and commit successfully.

other.title: Headroom may now be limited by something other than CPU in resolve
other.detail: Iterations 12 and 13 show per-link savings in Relationships.resolve() are giving less and less. Remaining CPU cost is register-time work (about 31k full getDescribe().getName() calls) and the unavoidable put. A per-SObjectType name cache (iteration 2 bundled one with semantic changes that broke tests) is still worth trying on its own.

other.title: Reformatting inflated the line count
other.detail: The DEFERRED changes were split over 3-4 lines (for example :283-286, :899-902). This does not affect coverage, which counts statements, but it hurts readability. Consider a private helper or a single-line form.

retro.head: e9abff15ac2cc4ad443a4361c35afb1efed48655
retro.summary: Only fflib_QueryFactory.cls changed, so it drove every score change. PMD (43.9→100) came from brace additions (#1) and suppressing OverrideBothEqualsAndHashcode on equals (#8). Graph Engine (75.8→100) came from a null-safe getFieldForType helper (#5). Limit headroom (57.3→88.1) came from a static field-path cache (#6) and a NONE-mode fast path in selectStringField (#11). Code coverage barely moved (93.1→93.5) because #10 and #15 reshaped code into ternaries instead of adding tests, and #10 assumed fflib_SObjectSelectorTest was deleted when it exists and covers USER_MODE/SYSTEM_MODE. Resource efficiency (98.8) did not move. No regression shows on tested paths; the risks are an unbounded static cache, a fast path that copies addField, one changed exception type, and code that is harder to read.

behaviourChanges.title: Static cross-instance cache of resolved field paths in NONE mode
behaviourChanges.detail: RESOLVED_FIELD_PATHS is a static Map that lives for the whole transaction, keyed by '<table>:<relatedType>:<fieldName>' with the field name in its original case. In NONE mode, a later factory gets the cached canonical path and skips fflib_SObjectDescribe. The result is the same because describe results are fixed within a transaction and NONE mode does no per-call checks. Failed resolutions are never cached, so invalid fields still throw each time. Side effects: the map never shrinks, so heap grows with every distinct table, field and casing seen in a long transaction or batch. Each casing variant gets its own entry. fflib_SObjectDescribe.flushCache() does not clear this map. LEGACY, USER_MODE and SYSTEM_MODE never read it.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In NONE mode, select 'name', 'NAME' and 'Owner.Name' on one factory, then build a second factory on the same table and select the same names. Assert that both give the same fields and SOQL, and that a later selectField('bogus__c') still throws InvalidFieldException.

behaviourChanges.title: NONE-mode fast path bypasses addField
behaviourChanges.detail: In NONE mode, selectStringField writes straight to fields.add(...) and builds the cache key itself (table + ':null:'), so it copies both addField's NONE-mode rule and getFieldPath's key format. Both copies are equivalent today. If addField starts normalising paths, or the key format changes, the fast path will drift silently: it will either always miss the cache or add paths that addField would have changed. selectField(String), selectFields(Set) and selectFields(List) all take this path. selectFieldSet, selectSObjectFields and selectField(String, SObjectType) still go through addField.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In NONE mode, select the same field through selectField('Name'), selectFields(Set{'name'}), selectField(Account.Name) and a field set. Assert that getSelectedFields() contains exactly one 'Name' entry, so all entry points produce the same path.

behaviourChanges.title: Ordering(String sobjType, ...) with an unknown or blank SObject name now throws InvalidFieldException instead of NullPointerException
behaviourChanges.detail: Before, fflib_SObjectDescribe.getDescribe(sobjType) returned null and .getField threw a NullPointerException. Now getFieldForType returns null, and getFieldTokenPath(null) throws InvalidFieldException('Invalid field: null'). This is arguably better, but the exception type changed, and the message no longer names the bad SObject type. Callers that catch NullPointerException will no longer catch it.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Construct new fflib_QueryFactory.Ordering('NotAnObject__x', 'Name', ASCENDING) and assert that it throws fflib_QueryFactory.InvalidFieldException.

behaviourChanges.title: Polymorphic relationship resolution rewritten as ternaries
behaviourChanges.detail: The old code used relatedObjs[0] when there was one target or relatedSObjectType was null. Otherwise it looped to the first match and left lastSObjectType unchanged if nothing matched. The new code uses contains() and two ternaries and is logically equivalent, including the old quirk where a non-matching relatedSObjectType leaves lastSObjectType as the current object. Nothing in the suite runs the non-null relatedSObjectType path on a dotted field, so an error here would not be caught. The cache key includes relatedSObjectType, so caching this path is safe.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: On Task, call selectField('What.Name', Account.SObjectType) and assert that the path is 'What.Name'. Call selectField('Owner.Username', User.SObjectType) on Lead and assert that it resolves, and that selectField('Owner.Username', Group.SObjectType) throws InvalidFieldException.

behaviourChanges.title: USER_MODE/SYSTEM_MODE handling restructured but equivalent
behaviourChanges.detail: getFieldPath's early return, addField's lowercasing and the WITH USER_MODE/SYSTEM_MODE clause in toSOQL are now always-evaluated ternaries. The output is unchanged for all four modes, and subselects still get no mode clause. Every call in the hot path now pays for the extra evaluation; #10's own learning measured about -2.5 headroom.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Already covered by fflib_SObjectSelectorTest.cls:453,469,483-486 and the USER_MODE assertion at 873.

patterns.title: Braces on every if/else/for
patterns.detail: A mechanical PMD fix that does not change behaviour.

patterns.title: Memoizing deterministic describe resolution, gated by FLS mode
patterns.detail: A sound optimisation that keeps LEGACY's per-call readable checks. Weaknesses: the cache is unbounded, it is keyed by the raw caller-supplied case, and its key format exists as two separate string literals.

patterns.title: Duplicated fast path that skips addField
patterns.detail: It copies addField and getFieldPath behaviour into selectStringField, so there are now two code paths to keep in step.

patterns.title: Folding if-bodies into always-run ternaries to game line coverage
patterns.detail: These edits make the code harder to read, do work on every call even when the branch is irrelevant, and produced little or no coverage gain. Iteration 10 was also justified by a test class 'being deleted' when it exists.

patterns.title: @SuppressWarnings('PMD.OverrideBothEqualsAndHashcode') on equals
patterns.detail: This hides a real contract violation: equal factories can have different hashCodes, which makes Set and Map behaviour inconsistent. It was done because the deterministic_toSOQL test relies on that inconsistency.

patterns.title: Explanatory comment on the cost of LEGACY FLS removed
patterns.detail: The deleted comment explained why native modes skip resolution and that LEGACY is planned for removal. That design context is now gone.

patterns.title: Top-level static helper for a null-safe describe lookup
patterns.detail: A small, clear null guard that replaces an NPE with a domain exception.

testGaps.title: Cache reuse across factories and casings
testGaps.detail: Nothing checks that a second factory, or a different casing, gets the same canonical path from the cache, or that invalid fields still throw after a successful lookup on the same table.
testGaps.proposedTest: Build two NONE factories on Contact and select 'lastname', 'LASTNAME', 'Account.Name' on each. Assert identical toSOQL(). Then assert that selectField('Account.Bogus') throws InvalidFieldException.

testGaps.title: Polymorphic selectField(String, SObjectType) on dotted paths
testGaps.detail: No test passes a non-null relatedSObjectType with a cross-object field, so the rewritten branch at 171-179 never runs.
testGaps.proposedTest: On Task in NONE and LEGACY modes, call selectField('What.Name', Account.SObjectType) and selectField('Owner.Username', User.SObjectType), and assert the resolved paths.

testGaps.title: Ordering with an invalid SObject name
testGaps.detail: The new null guard and the changed exception type are not checked.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that new Ordering('Nope__x', 'Name', ASCENDING) throws InvalidFieldException.

testGaps.title: OFFSET in toSOQL
testGaps.detail: No test sets an offset, so the OFFSET branch never runs.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call setLimit(10).setOffset(5) and assert that toSOQL() ends with ' LIMIT 10 OFFSET 5'.

testGaps.title: Mode clause on subselects
testGaps.detail: The ternary path that drops WITH USER_MODE/SYSTEM_MODE when relationship != null is only covered indirectly.
testGaps.proposedTest: Set USER_MODE on an Account factory with a Contacts subselect. Assert that 'WITH USER_MODE' appears exactly once, after FROM Account.

other.title: Faulty premise in the iteration log
other.detail: Iteration 10 says fflib_SObjectSelectorTest is deleted, but sfdx-source/apex-common/test/classes/fflib_SObjectSelectorTest.cls exists and runs SYSTEM_MODE and USER_MODE. Either the coverage run left it out, or the planner was misinformed. Check how coverage is measured before trusting the coverage scores.

other.title: Headroom test favours caching
other.detail: headroomBulkQueryBuilding repeats the same (table, field) pairs thousands of times, so it rewards memoization strongly. Real selectors build a few factories per transaction and will gain much less, while still paying the heap cost of the static map.

retro.head: b8fc1f112ec984e5ab6ab7d92a170c467f6a35d4
retro.summary: Only fflib_SObjectSelector.cls changed. PMD went from 49 to 100 through brace wraps and the DEFERRED describe option (iterations 3, 5, 9, 10). Coverage went from 83.6 to 90.8 by wiring uncalled public methods into paths that already run (iterations 13, 15), not by adding tests. Limit headroom ended 1 point below the baseline even though iterations 9 and 19 added static describe, field-name and default-order-by caches. Normal behaviour is preserved. The main change is that the DescribeSObjectResult (and so isAccessible()) is now cached per transaction instead of per selector, which can give stale CRUD answers across System.runAs.

behaviourChanges.title: Object describe and isAccessible() now cached per transaction, not per selector
behaviourChanges.detail: The sObjectDescribe getter now reads a static SOBJECT_DESCRIBE_CACHE keyed by SObjectType. In the baseline, each new selector instance ran a fresh getDescribe(), so a selector built inside System.runAs saw the runAs user's object access. Now the first describe of a type in the transaction is reused by every later selector, whichever user is running. Public assertIsAccessible() can then pass or fail based on another user's permissions. The CrudException catch is safe because its fallback throw sends the same message either way. In production the running user doesn't change within a transaction, so the risk is mostly tests and code that use System.runAs.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In one test method, outside runAs, call new AccountSelector().assertIsAccessible() (passes as admin). Then, inside runAs with a user who has no Account read access, call new AccountSelector().assertIsAccessible() and assert it throws DomainException. With the static cache it doesn't throw.

behaviourChanges.title: Describe fetched with SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED
behaviourChanges.detail: Child relationships load lazily. The selector never reads them from this describe, so there is no visible change. If someone later adds getChildRelationships() through sObjectDescribe, it still works, just loaded lazily.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Not needed. Optionally assert getSObjectName() and the CurrencyIsoCode detection give the same results as an EAGER describe.

behaviourChanges.title: Default getOrderBy() string cached per SObjectType for the transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: The name field, its encryption flag and whether CreatedDate exists are schema facts, so the result matches the baseline. Overridden getOrderBy() and the per-instance m_orderBy behave as before. The fallback branch now reads the shared cached describe instead of the instance's sObjectFieldsMap, which gives the same answer.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Assert the default getOrderBy() for an object with no name field or an encrypted one (for example a custom object with an AutoNumber or encrypted Name) returns CreatedDate or Id. Today only name-field objects are exercised.

behaviourChanges.title: Constructor routes through setDataAccess
behaviourChanges.detail: Same end state: non-LEGACY modes only come from the (Boolean, DataAccess) constructor, which already passes enforceCRUD and enforceFLS as false, and null access also leaves both false. setDataAccess is non-virtual, so subclasses can't intercept it during construction.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Assert isEnforcingCRUD() and isEnforcingFLS() are false for USER_MODE and SYSTEM_MODE selectors, and true or false as passed for LEGACY selectors.

behaviourChanges.title: Extra assertIsAccessible() call in the CRUD catch
behaviourChanges.detail: It throws the same DomainException message as the fallback, so callers see no difference. It adds a describe lookup on the failure path only. The fallback throw stays as a backstop that, in practice, only runs when the cached describe disagrees with the live check.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Covered by testAssertIsAccessible. Optionally assert the exception type and message exactly.

patterns.title: Brace wraps with redundant branches kept
patterns.detail: Pure readability and PMD fixes. Keeping the redundant null and ASC sort branches preserved behaviour and coverage.

patterns.title: Static per-transaction caches of schema-only values
patterns.detail: FIELD_NAME_CACHE and DEFAULT_ORDER_BY_CACHE hold values that depend only on the key, so they are safe. SOBJECT_DESCRIBE_CACHE also holds the user-dependent isAccessible(), which makes it less safe than it looks.

patterns.title: Coverage bought by wiring uncalled public methods into covered paths
patterns.detail: getSObjectType2 calling sObjectType(), the constructor calling setDataAccess, and the catch calling assertIsAccessible() raise line coverage without testing those methods' contracts. The catch now does the same check twice, and its fallback throw is effectively dead code.

patterns.title: Hill climbing gated on a noisy headroom metric
patterns.detail: Brace-only edits were rejected for headroom drops of 10-20 points, and the final headroom is below the baseline despite the caches. The metric's run-to-run noise is larger than the effects being measured.

testGaps.title: CRUD answers across System.runAs after describe caching
testGaps.detail: No test describes the same SObjectType as two different users in one transaction.
testGaps.proposedTest: Build an AccountSelector and call getSObjectName() as admin, then call assertIsAccessible() inside runAs with a user who has no Account read access. Expect DomainException.

testGaps.title: Default order-by fallback branch
testGaps.detail: The CreatedDate and Id branches of resolveDefaultOrderBy aren't asserted for any object.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a selector on an object without a usable name field and assert getOrderBy() equals 'CreatedDate', or 'Id' when CreatedDate is missing.

testGaps.title: Public methods covered only indirectly
testGaps.detail: setDataAccess, ignoreCRUD, sObjectType and assertIsAccessible run without any assertions on what they do.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call setDataAccess(USER_MODE) on a LEGACY selector built with enforceCRUD=true and assert isEnforcingCRUD() and isEnforcingFLS() become false. Call ignoreCRUD() and assert isEnforcingCRUD() is false.

testGaps.title: Multi-currency CurrencyIsoCode selection
testGaps.detail: The CURRENCY_ISO_CODE_ENABLED path, now backed by the cached describe, never runs in a single-currency scratch org.
testGaps.proposedTest: Add a multi-currency scratch definition and assert CurrencyIsoCode appears in the generated SOQL.

other.title: Possible later cleanup
other.detail: If SOBJECT_DESCRIBE_CACHE is kept, consider dropping the redundant fallback throw in the CrudException catch, or reverting assertIsAccessible() to a per-instance describe so the access check is always fresh. Iteration 21 showed that per-build describes aren't a meaningful CPU cost.

other.title: Gains came from a few iterations
other.detail: Of 24 iterations, 7 were kept. PMD came from iterations 3, 5, 9 and 10, coverage from 13 and 15, and headroom only from 19 (+4.7, which still left the final score below the baseline).

retro.head: 3d17d97ce47732c7e3790b25d0f4cbf6c97512e0
retro.summary: Only fflib_Application.cls changed. PMD (28.1→100) came from braces in #2 and a class-wide debug-statement suppression in #4. Limit headroom (60.6→85) came from Id-type caches in selectById (#6, #7) and a snapshot cache in selectByRelationship (#13), both tuned to a benchmark that sends the same list 320 times. Coverage (90.1→98.8) came only from restructuring (#9–#12, #15, #16), so the gain does not mean more is tested. Most edits behave the same as the baseline; the two caches are the real risk, because they keep data for the whole transaction and add CPU and heap cost for typical callers that pass a new list each time.

behaviourChanges.title: selectByRelationship compares and deep-clones the input list on every new list
behaviourChanges.detail: Every call compares the list field by field (List<SObject> !=) against a saved deepClone(true,true,true). A new list, which is the normal case, also gets cloned. Callers that pass each list once, such as triggers or services, now pay extra CPU and roughly double the heap for that list, and the factory, often a static field, holds the copy for the whole transaction. A large batch scope or a list with many fields could hit the heap limit, and the baseline never did this. Results stay correct, because any field difference causes a miss and the cache only supplies the Id set.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call selectByRelationship with 5,000 records with several fields populated, each a new list, and assert Limits.getHeapSize() and CPU stay within a fixed limit relative to the baseline loop; also call it with the same list after changing one AccountId and assert the new Id is passed to the selector.

behaviourChanges.title: selectById keeps every checked Id for the transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: m_validatedIdsBySObjectType keeps all checked Ids for each SObjectType. The reset is checked before addAll (size() > 10000), so one large call can push the set well past 10,000 Ids, and the set is never released. Every call that misses also loops over every cached type with containsAll before falling back to the full check. Results and exceptions are unchanged, because an Id's type never changes and a mixed-type set can never be fully contained in a single-type set.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call selectById with a 20,000-Id set, then with a different 100-Id set, and assert heap growth is bounded; check a mixed-type set still throws 'Unable to determine SObjectType' after a single-type subset was cached.

behaviourChanges.title: New protected field exposed to subclasses
behaviourChanges.detail: m_validatedIdsBySObjectType is @NamespaceAccessible protected, so subclasses can see and change it. A subclass that adds wrong Ids could make selectById use the wrong SObjectType without checking.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Make the field private, or add a test proving a subclass cannot bypass the type check.

behaviourChanges.title: DomainFactory construction order changed slightly
behaviourChanges.detail: The SObjectType constructor now chains through this(selectorFactory, new Map<Object,Type>()), so mockDomainByObject and an empty constructorTypeByObject are set before the overridable getConstructorTypeByObject runs. In the baseline, constructorTypeByObject was null at that point. A subclass that reads these fields inside its override would see different values. Construction also creates one extra throwaway Map.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Subclass DomainFactory, override getConstructorTypeByObject to record whether constructorTypeByObject and mockDomainByObject are null, and assert the expected state.

behaviourChanges.title: Domain constructor dispatch relies on IConstructable2 extending IConstructable
behaviourChanges.detail: The new early guard sends anything that is not IConstructable to the fflib_IDomainConstructor cast. This matches the baseline only because IConstructable2 extends IConstructable. If that relationship changed, IConstructable2-only classes would throw TypeException. The path for classes implementing only the old IConstructable interface is still never run by any test.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Register a constructor class that implements only fflib_SObjectDomain.IConstructable, and assert DomainFactory.newInstance returns its domain built from the records.

patterns.title: Caches tuned to the benchmark
patterns.detail: The selectByRelationship snapshot cache only helps when the same value-equal list is passed again, which the headroom test does 320 times and real code rarely does. Iteration #13 helps the benchmark and makes normal use slower.

patterns.title: Coverage raised by restructuring code, not by adding tests
patterns.detail: Ternaries fold if/return bodies onto one line (#11, #15), constructors chain to empty ones (#10, #12), and helpers add executed lines (#9, #16). This raised the coverage ratio while the IConstructable path, the non-mock unit-of-work paths and setMock(fflib_IDomain) stay untested. Readability also suffers: construct2 and the short isV2/recs/ctor names exist only to keep a line under the formatter's width limit.

patterns.title: Class-wide PMD.AvoidDebugStatements suppression
patterns.detail: This hides any debug statement added to the class in future, not just the two intended setMock warnings. A method-level @SuppressWarnings on the two setMock methods would be tighter.

patterns.title: Braces on all if/for bodies
patterns.detail: A pure syntax change that removes the risk of mistakes with unbraced bodies.

patterns.title: Cache invalidation by value equality
patterns.detail: #13 validates the cache by comparing against a deep-cloned snapshot and hands out a cloned Id set, so callers can't corrupt it. It is safe, but it is costly to run on every call.

testGaps.title: IConstructable (v1-only) domain constructor path
testGaps.detail: No test constructor implements only IConstructable; #15 hid that path on a line that always runs.
testGaps.proposedTest: Register a class implementing only IConstructable, and assert newInstance(records) returns its domain with the same records.

testGaps.title: UnitOfWorkFactory without a mock
testGaps.detail: All four newInstance overloads are only tested after setMock.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call each newInstance overload without setMock and assert the result is an fflib_SObjectUnitOfWork with the expected object types and IDML.

testGaps.title: selectByRelationship cache invalidation
testGaps.detail: No test calls it twice with the same list after changing a row, with a different field, or after setMock was called between the calls.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call it, change one record's AccountId, call it again, and assert the mock selector receives the new Id set; repeat with a different relationship field and after registering a mock selector.

testGaps.title: selectById cache with mixed and overlapping sets
testGaps.detail: Only the always-mixed set case is tested. No test passes a mixed-type set after a single-type set was cached.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call selectById with Account Ids, then with those Ids plus one Opportunity Id, and assert DeveloperException 'Unable to determine SObjectType...'.

testGaps.title: setMock(fflib_IDomain) and the Map<Object,Type> DomainFactory constructor
testGaps.detail: Both are unreachable from the current tests.
testGaps.proposedTest: Build a DomainFactory with Map<Object,Type>, register a mock using a variable typed as fflib_IDomain, and assert newInstance returns it for that getType() key.

testGaps.title: Volume and heap behaviour
testGaps.detail: The only headroom test reuses one 400-row list; it does not measure large or new lists.
testGaps.proposedTest: Add a headroom test that passes 50 new 2,000-row lists to selectByRelationship and asserts heap and CPU stay bounded.

other.title: Iteration #1's lesson was probably wrong
other.detail: #1 was discarded because removing the two setMock System.debug calls supposedly cost 8 headroom points, but the headroom test never calls setMock. The drop was noise, and later iterations (#4, #8, #11, #19) show swings of about ±10 on edits that don't affect runtime cost. The margins may be too tight compared to the measurement noise.

other.title: Headroom is now limited by the test itself
other.detail: Iterations #14-#19 found that the remaining CPU is mostly the test's own loops, so further headroom gains here would mostly come from fitting the benchmark more closely. Consider removing or narrowing the #13 cache, and keeping the #7 cache only if real callers repeat selectById calls on overlapping sets.

retro.head: e495f52f8ae7dd4cc63b24b5d4a6a120fe308bba
retro.summary: Only fflib_SObjectDomain.cls changed, and the evolved code behaves the same as the baseline. PMD went from 17 to 100 because all missing-brace violations were cleared (iterations 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13), with redundant else removed after branches that already return (iterations 11, 13), so the checks keep their original order and still stop at the first match. Limit headroom went from 55 to 67.4 almost entirely because of iteration 15: getChangedRecords now reads the ExistingRecords getter once and uses the typed newRecord.Id. Coverage, Graph Engine and Resource efficiency did not move; Resource efficiency is measured on test classes that never run this class, so it could not reflect these edits.

behaviourChanges.title: ExistingRecords lazy getter now runs even when Records is empty
behaviourChanges.detail: Both getChangedRecords overloads read this.ExistingRecords once before the loop. In the baseline the getter ran only inside the loop, so a domain with no records never triggered the lazy load from Test.Database.oldRecords or Trigger.oldMap. The evolved code loads and caches the map on the first getChangedRecords call even with zero records. The value is the same as any later read would give, so the visible result (an empty list) does not change. Only the timing of the first load and caching changes, which a subclass could see only if it reads the private cache or changes Test.Database between calls.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Build a domain with an empty list, call getChangedRecords, then call Test.Database.onUpdate with an old map. Assert that ExistingRecords reflects whatever caching behaviour is intended.

behaviourChanges.title: Typed newRecord.Id replaces dynamic get('Id') with a cast
behaviourChanges.detail: For any SObject, including generic SObject, .Id and (Id) get('Id') return the same value, and both return null for an unsaved record. A null Id still fails containsKey and the record is skipped. This is equivalent; listed for completeness.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Add an unsaved record (no Id) to Records and assert it is not returned as changed.

behaviourChanges.title: Trigger dispatch moved from if/else-if to braced ifs that return early
behaviourChanges.detail: Each branch returns straight after its handler, and the after branch is reached only when isBefore is false, so it is equivalent to the baseline even if more than one operation flag is true. With no flag set, domainObject is still null and throws the same null-pointer error at :481 as before. The isEnabled rewrite falls through to return true exactly as the baseline did.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Through Test.Database or a direct triggerHandler call, set isBefore together with isUndelete and assert that no handler runs. Set isInsert and isUpdate together and assert that only the insert handler runs.

patterns.title: Braces on every if/for body
patterns.detail: Reduces the risk of dangling-statement bugs and cleared every PMD brace violation without changing logic.

patterns.title: Removing else after branches that return, to satisfy PMD
patterns.detail: Correct in both places only because every branch returns, so the checks still stop at the first match. The early-return dispatch reads less symmetrically than an else-if chain, and the safety depends on the return lines staying. Iteration 12, which dropped else without returning, shows how easily a later edit could break that.

patterns.title: Reading a property getter into a local before the loop
patterns.detail: Cuts repeated getter calls in a loop that runs once per record, with the same result because the getter only fills itself once.

patterns.title: Choosing edits by line count and coverage arithmetic
patterns.detail: Several plans kept or added lines only to protect the coverage score (for example, rejecting ternaries in iteration 10 and the single-get change in iteration 14). This made the climb favour layout over clarity, although the code that was kept is fine.

testGaps.title: Dispatch when more than one operation flag is set, or none
testGaps.detail: No test pins the rule that exactly one handler runs, or what happens when no flag is set.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call the triggerHandler path through a test domain that records which handlers ran. Assert that only one runs with isInsert and isUpdate both true, and that a null-pointer error or a defined error is raised when all flags are false.

testGaps.title: getChangedRecords edge cases
testGaps.detail: The tests cover only the normal case where every record is in the old map. Not covered: a null old map, a new record missing from the old map, and an unsaved record with no Id.
testGaps.proposedTest: With ExistingRecords null, assert an empty result. With one new record whose Id is not in the old map, assert it is excluded. With an unsaved record, assert it is excluded.

testGaps.title: isEnabled for every combination
testGaps.detail: Disabling each individual event is not systematically tested, so a reordering or dropped return in isEnabled could go unnoticed.
testGaps.proposedTest: For each of the 7 before/after and operation combinations, disable only that event and assert that its handler is skipped while the others still run.

other.title: Resource efficiency cannot see this class
other.detail: fflib_SObjectSelectorTest and fflib_ApplicationTest never run fflib_SObjectDomain, yet changes on that dimension decided several discards (iterations 3, 5). Those discards were noise rather than evidence about the edits.

other.title: triggerHandler is at its NcssCount limit
other.detail: Iteration 16 showed that adding any statement to triggerHandler triggers a PMD NcssCount violation. Future work there should first move logic out into helper methods.

retro.head: 6717c6e8ab2d5ca5a1f465d750afae81cda201ee
retro.summary: Only iterations 1 and 2 were kept, both PMD-only cleanups in fflib_SObjects.cls (the only class climbed), which drove PMD from 35.2 to 100. Behaviour is effectively unchanged: the hoisted loop bound matches the old `j = records.size()`, the added braces change nothing, and the DEFERRED describe only changes when child-relationship metadata is loaded. Every other score held or moved within noise; fflib_SObjectsTest.headroomBulkFieldOperations headroom (60.1→58.8) and fflib_SObjectDomainTest resource efficiency (80.9→78.3) dipped slightly, and iterations 3-5, which targeted headroom, were all discarded.

behaviourChanges.title: Constructor describe switched to SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED
behaviourChanges.detail: sObjectDescribe is a public property. Consumers that read child relationships or other heavy describe data from it now trigger lazy loading instead of reading pre-loaded data. The values are identical, so only when the describe cost is paid changes. Within the repo only getSObjectType() reads it.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Construct fflib_SObjects over Account and assert sObjectDescribe.getChildRelationships() is non-empty and equals Account.SObjectType.getDescribe().getChildRelationships().size().

behaviourChanges.title: Loop bound read once before the loop
behaviourChanges.detail: Equivalent to the baseline, which also captured records.size() once in `j`. If a subclass's getRecords() returned a list that grows during the loop, both versions would ignore the added records, so there is no new risk.
behaviourChanges.evidence: fflib_SObjects.cls:97-98, :113-114, :497-498 and the other loop headers
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: No test needed; behaviour is identical to the baseline.

patterns.title: Hoisted recordCount local for indexed loops
patterns.detail: Clears OneDeclarationPerLine and keeps the same CPU profile as the baseline.

patterns.title: Braces on all if statements
patterns.detail: Removes the dangling-statement hazard and changes no behaviour.

patterns.title: Spelling change made only to satisfy PMD
patterns.detail: The Schema. qualifier was dropped only because the PMD rule matches source text. It is harmless but cosmetic, and other qualified spellings elsewhere could be flagged again.

testGaps.title: Contents of the public sObjectDescribe are not tested
testGaps.detail: No test checks that the describe exposed through the property is complete after the switch to DEFERRED.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert sObjectDescribe.getName(), fields.getMap().size() and getChildRelationships().size() match a full Account describe.

testGaps.title: Blank checks on non-String fields
testGaps.detail: The getRecordsWith*BlankFieldValues methods rely on String.valueOf for Number, Boolean and Date fields. Iteration 3 nearly rewrote this logic, so it is the most likely place for a future regression.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use records with null, 0 and false values in NumberOfEmployees and a checkbox field, and assert each of the four methods' results, including that 0 and false count as not blank.

testGaps.title: setFieldValueByMap with null values map or key mapped to null
testGaps.detail: Iteration 3 depended on the semantics of `if (values?.containsKey(...))` when values is null, but the tests do not pin this down.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that a null map throws a NullPointerException, and that a key mapped to null sets the field to null.

other.title: Inconsistent headroom baseline
other.detail: The top-level Limit headroom baseline is 57.3, but its only headroom test scored 60.1 at baseline, so the reported +1.5 is really a -1.3. Check how the baseline is aggregated before trusting headroom deltas.

other.title: Learnings from the discarded headroom attempts
other.detail: Iterations 3-5 showed that CPU in headroomBulkFieldOperations is dominated by SObject get/put calls and allocations. Loop restructuring, cached casts and post-hoc Set.remove calls did not help or made it worse. Future work should cut the number of field accesses or passes.

retro.head: be85edb05b3bfd1bd8178ed718556363364c603a
retro.summary: Only fflib_Objects.cls changed. Iteration 1 drove PMD (51→100) by adding braces and Limit headroom (57.6→90) by replacing a linear list search per value with a Set lookup. Iteration 2 drove Code coverage (90.5→100) by folding the null-guard returns onto one line, which hides untested lines rather than testing them. Resource efficiency barely moved because fflib_SObjects never calls the changed methods (fflib_SObjectsTest fell 1.0 and fflib_SObjectDomainTest rose 1.0, both noise), and results for normal inputs are unchanged.

behaviourChanges.title: Membership now uses hashCode plus equals instead of equals only
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline matched values with List.contains, which uses only equals(). The evolved code uses Set.containsAll and retainAll, which bucket by hashCode() first. Objects that override equals without a matching hashCode, or whose hashCode is inconsistent, can stop matching. SObjects and plain objects (compared by reference) behave the same.
behaviourChanges.evidence: sfdx-source/apex-common/main/classes/fflib_Objects.cls:61,66,84-88; the test DTO overrides neither method (fflib_ObjectsTest.cls:250)
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Add a value class that overrides equals and hashCode by a key field, build a domain from instances, and check containsAll and containsNot with distinct but equal instances.

behaviourChanges.title: Null internal list combined with an empty input now throws
behaviourChanges.detail: A subclass can null the list through setObjects(null). The baseline then returned true for containsAll(empty set) and containsNot(empty set) because the loop never ran. Now new Set<Object>(null) and retainAll(null) most likely throw. With a non-empty input, both versions already threw.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In a test subclass that calls setObjects(null), assert what containsAll(new Set<Object>()) and containsNot(new Set<Object>()) should do.

behaviourChanges.title: No early exit and an allocation sized to the domain on every call
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline containsAll stopped at the first missing value and allocated nothing. Now every call copies the whole object list into a new Set, and containsNot(List) copies its input twice. Frequent small checks against large domains now cost more heap and CPU per call, though cost stays linear.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Add a headroom test with a 10k-element domain that calls containsAll with a single missing value many times, and check Limits.getHeapSize and Limits.getCpuTime.

patterns.title: Braces on every if
patterns.detail: Cleared all 12 PMD findings with no change in behaviour.

patterns.title: Native Set operations instead of per-value loops
patterns.detail: Clearer code and a faster bulk case, but it quietly changes how equality is checked.

patterns.title: Guards folded into one-line boolean returns to raise coverage
patterns.detail: The null branches are still untested. Coverage rose only because they now share a line with tested code.

patterns.title: Defensive copy in containsNone
patterns.detail: retainAll runs on a copy, so the caller's Set is never changed.
patterns.evidence: fflib_Objects.cls:85; iteration 3 discarded the version that dropped the copy

patterns.title: Duplicated body instead of delegating
patterns.detail: containsAll(List) repeats the containsAll(Set) one-liner instead of calling it. Harmless while neither method is virtual.

testGaps.title: Null inputs
testGaps.detail: No test passes null to containsAll or containsNot, so the expected results (false and true) are not pinned down.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that containsAll((List<Object>) null) and containsAll((Set<Object>) null) return false, and that containsNot((List<Object>) null) and containsNot((Set<Object>) null) return true.

testGaps.title: Empty inputs and small mixed cases
testGaps.detail: No test uses an empty list or Set, an empty domain, or a small mix of present and absent values.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that containsAll(empty) is true, containsNot(empty) is true, containsAll([A, D]) is false, containsNot([A, D]) is false, and that an empty domain gives containsAll([A]) false and containsNot([A]) true.

testGaps.title: Custom equals and hashCode
testGaps.detail: Hashing changes behaviour for value objects, and nothing tests it.
testGaps.proposedTest: Build a domain of value objects that override equals and hashCode, then check contains, containsAll and containsNot with equal but distinct instances.

testGaps.title: Null internal list
testGaps.detail: What happens after setObjects(null) is not defined anywhere.
testGaps.proposedTest: In a subclass that calls setObjects(null), assert the expected exception or result for each containment method with empty and non-empty inputs.

testGaps.title: Caller's input is left unchanged
testGaps.detail: No test checks that containsNot(Set) leaves its argument untouched.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call containsNot(s) on a domain that partly overlaps s, then assert that s.size() and its contents are unchanged.

other.title: Score movement in untouched classes is noise
other.detail: fflib_SObjects never calls containsAll or containsNot (its only contains call is on a local Set, fflib_SObjects.cls:330), so the shifts in the two test classes' Resource efficiency and the Test run time rise from 74.9 to 80.1 are probably run-to-run noise.

other.title: Lessons from the discarded iterations
other.detail: Iterations 3-5 show that one-off allocation trims and caches layered beside the existing check don't register, and that the cache cost PMD and coverage. Further gains would have to come from changes that remove per-element work in fflib_SObjects.

retro.head: c5b7379ddff3bb9d17f9fd5dd99494c5b5e09d73
retro.summary: Only fflib_StringBuilder.cls changed. Iteration 1 (braces) drove PMD from 64.1 to 100 and iteration 3 (direct buffer.add plus a static multi-currency flag) drove Limit headroom from 63.2 to 73.2; coverage, run time and resource efficiency barely moved (≤0.2, noise). Output is identical inside this repo, but iteration 3 makes the constructors skip the public virtual add(String), so a subscriber-org subclass that overrides add no longer sees field or CurrencyIsoCode entries. That silent API break is the main risk, and no test covers it.

behaviourChanges.title: Constructors skip the overridable add(String) hook
behaviourChanges.detail: In the baseline, the FieldListBuilder constructor called the virtual add(String) for each SObjectField and each FieldSetMember path, and MultiCurrencyFieldListBuilder did the same for 'CurrencyIsoCode'. The evolved code writes to the protected buffer directly. FieldListBuilder and CommaDelimitedListBuilder are public virtual and @NamespaceAccessible, and add is public virtual, so code outside the namespace can subclass and override add (for example to deduplicate, as the 'Create a distinct set of fields' comment at :139 suggests, or to filter or namespace-prefix fields). Those overrides are now bypassed for constructor-supplied values. Overrides of add(String) on an anonymous subclass of FieldListBuilder are affected; calls to add made after construction are not. Iteration 3 only checked this repo's source tree for overrides.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In a test, define a subclass of FieldListBuilder that overrides add(String) to record each call (or to drop duplicates). Construct it with fields including a duplicate and assert the override ran for every field. This fails on the evolved code.

behaviourChanges.title: Multi-currency flag read once per transaction at class load
behaviourChanges.detail: UserInfo.isMultiCurrencyOrganization() used to be called on each MultiCurrencyFieldListBuilder construction. It is now evaluated once, when the class first loads in a transaction, for every user of the class (including plain StringBuilder use). The org setting can't change within a transaction, so output is the same. The costs are one extra system call in transactions that never build a multi-currency list, and less room to test both branches: the value is a private static final, so a test can't switch it.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Assert that MultiCurrencyFieldListBuilder output contains 'CurrencyIsoCode' if and only if UserInfo.isMultiCurrencyOrganization() is true (the current test only checks the positive case).

behaviourChanges.title: Brace addition
behaviourChanges.detail: This was a purely syntactic change and the semantics are the same. A null values list still throws a NullPointerException and fieldSets == null is still skipped.

patterns.title: Bypassing a virtual method from a constructor of an extensible class
patterns.detail: This gains CPU by skipping one call per field, at the cost of breaking the documented extension point of a public library class. A non-virtual private helper or a documented final contract would be a cleaner way to get the same speed-up.

patterns.title: Hoisting org-invariant system state into a top-level private static
patterns.detail: Reasonable for a value that can't change within a transaction. It had to sit on the top-level class because inner classes can't hold statics (iteration 2 failed to compile for this reason). It makes the branch harder to test.

patterns.title: Braces on all control statements
patterns.detail: Safe PMD cleanup.

patterns.title: Comment says 'distinct' but nothing deduplicates
patterns.detail: This predates the climb, but it hints that callers or subclasses are expected to deduplicate through add, which makes the iteration 3 bypass riskier. testFieldListBuilder passes a duplicate AccountNumber and compares only as a Set, so duplicates are tolerated.

testGaps.title: Subclass add() override contract
testGaps.detail: No test subclasses any builder, so constructor dispatch through add is not pinned down.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a recording subclass of FieldListBuilder, and of MultiCurrencyFieldListBuilder through FieldListBuilder, and assert that add(String) saw every constructor-supplied field.

testGaps.title: Field set paths
testGaps.detail: No test passes a non-null fieldSets list, so the FieldSetMember loop (:144-150) is unverified for ordering and content.
testGaps.proposedTest: If the org has an Account field set (or a packaged test fixture), build FieldListBuilder(fields, new List<Schema.FieldSet>{fs}) and assert the field paths follow the SObjectFields in order.

testGaps.title: Exact output and order
testGaps.detail: The tests compare as Sets, so changes to order or duplicates would pass unnoticed. Iteration 4's join/split did break tests, but only through other assertions.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert the exact string, e.g. 'Name,Id,AccountNumber,AnnualRevenue' for FieldListBuilder, and 'Parent.Name,Parent.Id' for getStringValue('Parent.').

testGaps.title: Null and empty inputs
testGaps.detail: Empty field lists and null values are not tested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that new FieldListBuilder(new List<SObjectField>()).getStringValue() == '' and that a null list throws a NullPointerException.

other.title: Headroom gains have plateaued
other.detail: Iterations 4 to 8 were all discarded. The remaining CPU is in String.valueOf per field and String.join. Further work here would mostly chase noise, given a 7.9 margin against changes of about 1 to 2 points.

other.title: Possible quick fix
other.detail: Restoring add(...) in the constructors while keeping the static flag would keep most of the safe gain and remove the API risk. Measure how much of iteration 3's +8 came from each part before deciding.

retro.head: 1b5082c5d85bfc8b61368809f8650980f2962696
retro.summary: The ascent changed only fflib_SObjectDescribe.cls. PMD (71.4→100) came from iterations 1–2 (for-each loops, deferred describe with an unqualified enum), coverage (95.5→98.8) from deleting unreachable or duplicate code in iterations 4–5, and resource efficiency (+2.4) from keying instanceCache by SObjectType in iteration 8. Limit headroom fell (73.7→59.1), most likely because getDescribe(String) now always goes through the global describe instead of checking the instance cache first, though this dimension is noisy (about ±12). Behaviour is preserved in single-namespace orgs; the only semantic shift is that namespace-omitted String lookups now return a cached, namespace-preferring instance.

behaviourChanges.title: getDescribe(String) always resolves through the global describe
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline checked instanceCache by lowercased name and only fell back to wrappedGlobalDescribe on a miss. The evolved code always calls wrappedGlobalDescribe.get(name). After flushCache(), a String lookup of an already-described type now rebuilds Schema.getGlobalDescribe() and the GlobalDescribeMap wrapper, and every String lookup pays the namespaced-key string work. The returned instance is the same; the cost is CPU and heap, and it likely explains the Limit headroom drop (73.7→59.1).
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: After flushCache(), call getDescribe(Account.SObjectType) then getDescribe('Account') and assert that Limits.getCpuTime() / heap growth stays under a bound, or at least that both calls return the same instance.

behaviourChanges.title: Namespace-omitted String lookups now hit the cache and consistently prefer the namespaced type
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline cache key was String.valueOf(token).toLowerCase() (for example 'ns__obj__c'), so getDescribe('Obj__c') in namespace ns never hit the cache, built a new instance on every call and overwrote the cache entry. When both an unmanaged Obj__c and a packaged ns__Obj__c existed, the baseline returned whichever matched a cached 'obj__c' key, otherwise the namespaced one. The evolved code always resolves through GlobalDescribeMap.get (namespace-preferred) and returns the cached instance: more consistent, but different.
behaviourChanges.evidence: fflib_SObjectDescribe.cls:255, :263, :395-406 (getObject namespace preference); baseline lines removed in the diff at the old :253-264
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Using the existing fakeNamespace technique on a GlobalDescribeMap, or in a namespaced scratch org, assert that getDescribe('Obj__c') === getDescribe(ns__Obj__c.SObjectType) and that repeated String calls return the same instance.

behaviourChanges.title: getNameField uses a DEFERRED describe with an unqualified enum
behaviourChanges.detail: fields.getMap() is identical under DEFERRED, so the returned name field does not change. The unqualified SObjectDescribeOptions reference would resolve to a local class if one with that name were ever added, which is a compile-time risk rather than a runtime one.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Already covered by getNameField_staticBasics (Account.Name, Contact.Name).

behaviourChanges.title: DescribeSObjectResult overload delegates to the token overload
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline looked up getName().toLowerCase(), which equals String.valueOf(token).toLowerCase(), so the delegation is equivalent and also drops redundant null-safe operators. No behaviour change, but instance identity for this overload is not asserted (the test is commented out).
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Uncomment the d4/d5 assertions in getAccountDescribes, using === rather than areEqual.

patterns.title: Deleting unreachable members and no-op branches to raise coverage
patterns.detail: The removed no-arg constructor, the one-arg getObject of a private abstract class and the `if (token == null) result = null` branch were all dead. Coverage rose by shrinking the denominator honestly.

patterns.title: Keying the cache by SObjectType instead of a derived string
patterns.detail: Simpler and cheaper, and it removes the namespace-dependent key mismatch, so String and token lookups share one instance.

patterns.title: Rewriting code to match PMD's literal pattern
patterns.detail: Dropping the Schema. qualifier only to satisfy the EagerlyLoadedDescribeSObjectResult rule's matcher is benign but tool-driven, and makes the code slightly less explicit than the rest of the file, which uses Schema.-qualified names.

patterns.title: Collapsing getDescribe(String) into a single delegation
patterns.detail: Cleaner, but it gives up the cheap cache-first path, so String callers now pay a global-describe lookup on every call. A cache-first check by token is not possible without the string key, so this is an explicit trade-off of CPU for simplicity.

patterns.title: for-each loops replacing indexed loops
patterns.detail: Equivalent semantics (a null list still throws NullPointerException) and clears the OneDeclarationPerLine finding.

testGaps.title: Instance identity across all getDescribe overloads
testGaps.detail: Only the String, SObjectType and Schema.SObjectType.Account forms are compared, and with areEqual rather than reference identity; the DescribeSObjectResult and SObject forms are commented out.
testGaps.proposedTest: In getAccountDescribes, assert getDescribe('account') === getDescribe(Account.SObjectType.getDescribe()) === getDescribe(new Account()) === getDescribe(Account.SObjectType).

testGaps.title: Unknown String name returns null
testGaps.detail: The null path now relies on GlobalDescribeMap.get returning null, then on the token overload's null guard. Only blank and null strings are tested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert getDescribe('NotARealObject__c') == null and getDescribe('NotARealObject__c') does not populate any cache (a follow-up getDescribe(Account.SObjectType) still works).

testGaps.title: Mixed-case and namespaced String resolution
testGaps.detail: Case-insensitivity and namespace preference in getDescribe(String) are untested now that it delegates entirely to GlobalDescribeMap.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert getDescribe('aCcOuNt') === getDescribe(Account.SObjectType); with gdm.currentNamespace set to a fake namespace, assert namespace-omitted lookups resolve to the namespaced token when both keys exist.

testGaps.title: Cost of String lookups after flushCache
testGaps.detail: No test pins the extra global-describe rebuild that String lookups now trigger.
testGaps.proposedTest: After flushCache, prime by token, then measure Limits.getCpuTime() across 100 getDescribe('Account') calls and assert it stays under a threshold derived from the baseline.

testGaps.title: getNameField on a type without a name field
testGaps.detail: The null return when no field has isNameField() is not exercised.
testGaps.proposedTest: Pick a standard object without a name field (for example a share or history type such as AccountHistory) and assert getNameField(type) == null.

other.title: Limit headroom delta may be partly noise
other.detail: Iteration 6 recorded a -12 swing on Limit headroom between two runs of the same code, so the 14.6-point drop is not entirely attributable to iteration 8. Re-measure before reverting.

other.title: Unmerged sub-margin wins
other.detail: Iterations 9–11 (caching the name field per instance and caching the namespace-stripped keySet) showed real CPU gains of about +11 to +15 headroom but missed the 23.3 margin. They are worth revisiting as a deliberate change outside the climb.

other.title: Stale doc comment
other.detail: The @deprecated note on getDescribe(String) at fflib_SObjectDescribe.cls:243-249 mentions dynamic Type resolution, but the method only uses the global describe map.

retro.head: d0b63be065d987267241e614f8717cb642fb4b1a
retro.summary: Only fflib_SObjectUnitOfWork changed. It drove PMD 43.9→100 (iteration 1), Code coverage 79.2→80.7 (iterations 3 and 7) and Limit headroom 59.9→71.2 in headroomBulkCommitWork (iterations 6–8). Resource efficiency barely moved: fflib_SObjectUnitOfWorkTest stayed at 94 and fflib_ApplicationTest went 81→80.9, which is noise. Iterations 1, 3, 6 and 8 are behaviour-equivalent apart from edge cases that can't happen in practice. The one real semantic change is iteration 7's per-type 'all resolved' cache in Relationships.resolve(), which makes the unit of work stateful across phases and across repeated commitWork calls.

behaviourChanges.title: Relationships.resolve() skips re-resolution once a pass fully resolves, including on later commitWork calls
behaviourChanges.detail: m_resolvedCount is set after a pass in which every relationship resolved, and it is never reset. Later passes in the same commit (the upsert and update phases) and every pass in a later commitWork on the same instance return early unless new relationships were added. In the baseline, any relationship whose lookup no longer equalled the parent Id was re-written with that Id in each phase. It now differs when (a) a resolved lookup field is changed between phases, e.g. by a custom IDML or an onDMLStarting/onRegisterType subclass hook, or (b) a caller reuses a unit of work, changes a child lookup or resets records after a failed or rolled-back commit, and calls commitWork again: the stale or edited value is kept instead of being overwritten with the parent Id. Incomplete passes (parent Id blank) are not cached, so the out-of-order and partial-failure retry paths still work.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Register a new Account and registerNew(opp, Opportunity.AccountId, acc), then commitWork with MockDML. Set opp.AccountId to a different generated Id, clear opp.Id, and commitWork again on the same uow. Assert that the second insert's AccountId equals acc.Id, as in the baseline.

behaviourChanges.title: Relationship.resolve now returns success; the completion signal for EmailRelationship and RelationshipByExternalId is always true
behaviourChanges.detail: EmailRelationship.resolve returns true even when relatedTo.Id is blank and WhatId is set to null. Combined with the cache, a second resolveEmailRelationships() in a reused unit of work no longer re-applies WhatId. Within a single commit, behaviour is unchanged.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Reuse a uow across two commitWork calls with registerRelationship(email, opp). Between commits, call email.setWhatId(null) and assert that WhatId equals opp.Id after the second commit.

behaviourChanges.title: registerDirty(record, field, parent) no longer re-validates against m_newListByType
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline validated the type against m_dirtyMapByType and then again against m_newListByType, through registerRelationship. Now only m_dirtyMapByType is checked before m_relationships.get(...). The maps are protected, so a subclass that edits them (e.g. in onRegisterType) so their keys differ now gets a NullPointerException, or a silent add, instead of UnitOfWorkException 'not supported'. With the stock handleRegisterType, the two maps always have the same keys.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In a derived unit of work, remove a type from m_relationships in onRegisterType. Assert that registerDirty(existing, field, parent) throws UnitOfWorkException rather than NullPointerException, or document that it doesn't.

behaviourChanges.title: assertForNonEventSObjectType edge semantics
behaviourChanges.detail: endsWithIgnoreCase('__e') equals the baseline check (Apex string == ignores case) except for the literal string '__e', which is not a real type name. assertForEventSObjectType still uses length/right, so the two helpers are now asymmetric.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call assertForNonEventSObjectType('My_Event__E') and assert it throws, to pin the case-insensitivity.

behaviourChanges.title: External-id registerRelationship exception now comes from the shared helper
behaviourChanges.detail: The exception type and message are identical; only the stack frame differs.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call registerRelationship(new Account(), Account.ParentId, Account.Id, 'x') on a uow without Account and assert the 'not supported' message.

behaviourChanges.title: DEFERRED describe in name-only lookups
behaviourChanges.detail: getName() is identical under SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED. There is no functional change, and the DEFERRED and eager describe results are not mixed in any one place.

patterns.title: Cache invalidation by list size
patterns.detail: The skip relies on m_relationships being append-only and on resolved lookups never being changed later. Both are unstated invariants, and the cache is never reset between commits.

patterns.title: Side-effecting call kept as the left operand of &&
patterns.detail: allResolved = relationship.resolve() && allResolved depends on operand order for correctness. It is correct, but easy to break by 'tidying' it.

patterns.title: Adding to Relationships directly after the caller has validated the type
patterns.detail: This removes a duplicate describe and asserts per call without changing order or messages, as long as the protected maps keep the same keys.

patterns.title: Reusing assertForSupportedSObjectType instead of a copied throw
patterns.detail: Removes duplicated code with an identical message.

patterns.title: Partial DEFERRED adoption
patterns.detail: Commit loops and handleRegisterType use DEFERRED, but the register methods (385, 411, 457, 501, 542) and the delete and recycle-bin loops (945, 957) still use the eager getDescribe(), presumably because PMD's rule misses the chained form. This is inconsistent style.

patterns.title: Asymmetric event-type helpers
patterns.detail: One helper uses endsWithIgnoreCase and the other uses length/right.

testGaps.title: Reusing a unit of work across commits
testGaps.detail: No test calls commitWork twice on one instance, so the persistent m_resolvedCount is untested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Commit twice with MockDML, changing the child lookup in between. Assert that the parent Id is re-applied.

testGaps.title: Lookup changed between the insert and update phases
testGaps.detail: No test changes a resolved field during commit, e.g. a custom IDML whose dmlInsert or dmlUpsert alters child lookups. The baseline re-resolved such fields in the update phase.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a custom IDML that nulls Opportunity.AccountId in dmlInsert for a dirty Opportunity registered with registerDirty(opp, AccountId, acc) when Opportunity is ordered after Account. Assert the updated record's AccountId.

testGaps.title: Parent supplied by the upsert phase
testGaps.detail: The cache is reached from the upsert phase, but no test has a dirty child whose parent only gets its Id from upsert.
testGaps.proposedTest: registerUpsert a new Account, registerDirty(existingOpp, Opportunity.AccountId, account) and commit. Assert the updated opp's AccountId equals account.Id.

testGaps.title: External-id relationship path
testGaps.detail: No test calls registerRelationship(record, field, externalIdField, value) or RelationshipByExternalId.resolve/isResolved.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use a custom object with an external-id field, or a test-only stub, and assert putSObject is populated and an unsupported type throws.

testGaps.title: headroomBulkCommitWork correctness
testGaps.detail: The bulk test measures limits but its correctness assertions weren't checked here. Ensure it asserts that resolved lookups appear on inserted and updated records at volume.
testGaps.proposedTest: After the bulk commit, assert every Task.WhoId equals its Contact Id and every dirty Opportunity.AccountId equals its Account Id.

other.title: Rejected ideas worth not retrying
